Explanation (added)

Property 1 says the cross product is anti-commutative: swapping the order flips the direction. In the triple scalar product the cross product must be done first — would be a number crossed with a vector, which means nothing — so the brackets are really only there for clarity. The identity says the dot and the cross can trade places.

Explanation (added)

Torque measures the tendency of the force to rotate the object about the origin of (the bolt). The magnitude formula is just : only the part of perpendicular to the handle, , turns the bolt. The direction of is the axis of rotation, given by the right-hand rule. In this picture, curling from to is clockwise, so points into the page (⊗). 04Planes: normal vectors and the vector equation

3 points in determine a plane.

Let .

Let be any vector that lies in the plane determined by .

Then and are orthogonal.

So .

Let be any point in the plane with normal vector (↳ a vector orthogonal to every vector in the plane) and containing the point .

Explanation (added)

The cross product of two vectors is perpendicular to both of them, so is perpendicular to the two edges and — and therefore to every vector built from them, which is every vector in the plane. (The three points must not all lie on one line, otherwise the cross product is and no single plane is determined.) A line needed a point and a direction; a plane needs a point and a normal.

What a typical exam question looks like

Questions on this material follow the examples above almost exactly:

  • “Find the volume of the parallelepiped determined by ”, or “show that the vectors are coplanar” (set up the determinant).
  • “Find a vector equation and parametric equations for the line through the point … parallel to the vector …” (or through two given points — the direction is then the difference of the points). Often followed by “find symmetric equations”.
  • “Find an equation of the plane through the point … with normal vector …”, and its intercepts with a sketch.
  • “Find an equation of the plane through the points , , ” — two difference vectors, a cross product, then the scalar equation.
  • “Find the point at which the line … intersects the plane …” — substitute the parametric equations into the plane and solve for .
  • “Find the torque / magnitude of the torque” for a force applied at the end of a wrench, given lengths and an angle.
